finding.claim: Stored SSRF: the callbackUrl a user submits to POST /subscribe is stored with no validation. The scheduled notifyAll job (every minute) later POSTs the payload to every stored URL. An attacker can register an internal or metadata URL such as http://169.254.169.254/ or http://localhost:8080/admin, and the server will send requests to it repeatedly. The impact is blind SSRF, because the response body is discarded. It still allows internal probing and port scanning, and it can reach internal POST endpoints. Java's HttpClient does not follow redirects by default, so redirect-based bypasses are not relevant, but the direct internal target is enough.
finding.source: callbackUrl body parameter of POST /subscribe (Jobs.subscribe, src/Jobs.java:13)

trace.note: subscribe(name, callbackUrl) receives the attacker-supplied URL from the POST /subscribe body
subscriptions.put(name, callbackUrl) stores it unvalidated in the static map
notifyAll iterates subscriptions.values() on the scheduled run, with no re-validation at fetch time
URI.create(cb) builds the request URI, so the user controls scheme, host and port
client.send(...) dispatches the POST to the attacker-chosen host

finding.guards_checked: No scheme or host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, and no re-validation at send time, either in subscribe or in notifyAll. No authentication is visible in this file, since the handler is only described by a comment. Redirects are not followed (HttpClient default is Redirect.NEVER), so that vector is closed. The response is not returned to the caller, so this is blind SSRF (MEDIUM to HIGH depending on whether the endpoint is authenticated). No in-repo CIDR egress config exists.

verdict.reason: src/Jobs.java:14 stores callbackUrl unvalidated and src/Jobs.java:21-24 sends a POST to it with no scheme, host or IP check. The only regex guard is in thumb() at line 30 and does not cover this path. No auth is visible, and the code is only shown as a comment at line 12, so the finding stands as blind SSRF.
